articles.title: Hóspede de Airbnb não será mais obrigado a lavar louça e tirar lixo | G1
articles.standfirst: Novas diretrizes da plataforma de hospedagem visam limitar as tarefas domésticas impostas aos viajantes. Anfitriões agora só podem impor tarefas consideradas "razoáveis".
articles.summary: Novas diretrizes da plataforma de hospedagem visam limitar as tarefas domésticas impostas aos viajantes. Anfitriões agora só podem impor tarefas consideradas "razoáveis".
articles.body:
Os anfitriões do Airbnb não poderão mais exigir que os hóspedes lavem a louça e a roupa de cama antes do check-out, conforme novas regras — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Os anfitriões do Airbnb não poderão mais exigir que os hóspedes lavem a louça e a roupa de cama antes do check-out, conforme novas regras que visam limitar as tarefas domésticas impostas aos viajantes.

A plataforma de hospedagem informou nesta semana que atualizou suas diretrizes: agora, os anfitriões só podem solicitar aos hóspedes a realização de tarefas consideradas "razoáveis".

Ainda é permitido, por exemplo, pedir que os hóspedes coloquem a louça suja na pia e reúnam as toalhas usadas. No entanto, os anfitriões não poderão mais exigir que os hóspedes levem o lixo para fora da propriedade.

"Os hóspedes não devem ser solicitados a levar o lixo para fora da propriedade, mas você pode pedir que separem o lixo dos materiais recicláveis em lixeiras internas específicas para cada tipo de resíduo", afirma a empresa em comunicado.

O Airbnb , contudo, abre margem para algumas exceções.

"Por exemplo, pode ser razoável pedir aos hóspedes que descartem o lixo em um recipiente à prova de animais – em regiões onde há ursos, por exemplo – ou solicitar que limitem o tempo de banho devido a restrições locais de água causadas pela seca."

Os hóspedes do Airbnb geralmente pagam uma taxa de limpeza. Por isso, a plataforma alerta os anfitriões de que "solicitar que realizem tarefas que caberiam a um profissional de limpeza pode afetar negativamente a estadia e as avaliações recebidas".

As mudanças entram em vigor no dia 20 de novembro.

As novas regras também proíbem que os anfitriões impeçam os hóspedes de utilizar comodidades listadas na descrição do imóvel, como o ar-condicionado.

articles.title: Fatal Custody
articles.summary: Two mothers warned family courts their children were in danger. Fault Lines investigates why warnings were ignored.
articles.body:
Hope Hooton and Kellie Elliott feared their children were not safe with their fathers. Hope sought protection after her husband threatened suicide and later experienced a psychiatric crisis. Kellie documented years of domestic violence and abuse. Yet both fathers had unsupervised time with their children, whom they later killed.

Through the stories of these two mothers, Fault Lines investigates how evidence of danger can be missed, dismissed or fail to reach family courts at all. The film examines the push for equal custody, the failure to treat violence against a parent as a risk to children and the changes advocates say could prevent other families from suffering the same losses.

articles.title: Cidade que atingiu 45 °C terá médicos em locais de votação no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Profissionais ficarão de prontidão em cinco bairros de Teresina no segundo turno das eleições, no domingo (25). Eleitores devem levar água e usar roupas leves para enfrentar o calor.
articles.summary: Profissionais ficarão de prontidão em cinco bairros de Teresina no segundo turno das eleições, no domingo (25). Eleitores devem levar água e usar roupas leves para enfrentar calor.
articles.body:
Local de votação em Teresina, no Piauí (imagem ilustrativa) — Foto: Aric Lages/g1

Teresina , capital do Piauí, terá médicos, enfermeiros e técnicos de enfermagem de prontidão em locais de votação considerados mais quentes durante o segundo turno das Eleições 2026, no domingo (25). Ao todo, 15 profissionais da saúde foram convocados pelo Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Piauí (TRE-PI) para atender eleitores e mesários que possam passar mal por causa das altas temperaturas.

No dia 7 de outubro, um termômetro da Prefeitura de Teresina registrou uma temperatura máxima de 45,22 °C em um bairro na zona Norte da capital. Nas demais áreas do município, as temperaturas também ultrapassaram 40 °C.

As equipes atuarão em seções eleitorais dos bairros Promorar , Esplanada , Vale Quem Tem , Ininga e Primavera . Os locais foram selecionados a partir do cruzamento de dados do Kiwi, simulador de filas desenvolvido pelo Cajuína Lab, que também identificou as regiões mais quentes da capital durante o primeiro turno.

Segundo Celeyda Motta, assessora de assistência à Saúde do TRE-PI, a medida busca prevenir e atender ocorrências relacionadas ao calor durante a votação.

“Nós estamos em pleno B-R-O-Bró e registrando temperaturas cada vez mais altas. Com base no mapeamento, nós convocamos profissionais da saúde para ficarem de prontidão para atender aqueles que possam sentir algum desconforto por causa do calor”, explicou.

🌡️B-R-O-Bró é uma expressão popular usada no Piauí para se referir ao período mais quente do ano, geralmente entre setembro e dezembro, quando as temperaturas costumam ser mais elevadas e o clima fica mais seco.

O calor excessivo pode provocar boca seca, cansaço, tontura, queda da pressão arterial, dor de cabeça, cãibras musculares, sudorese intensa e desmaios .

A iniciativa faz parte do Plano SALV-E (Suporte de Atendimento e Logística para a Vida), criado pelo TRE-PI para estabelecer protocolos de prevenção e resposta a emergências médicas, incluindo procedimentos de Suporte Básico de Vida, durante as eleições de 2026.

No primeiro turno, uma equipe do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) de Altos prestou atendimento a mesários e eleitores na Unidade Escolar Maria Raulino e na Escola Pio XXII.

O TRE-PI recomenda que eleitores e mesários levem água para consumo individual, mantenham-se hidratados ao longo do dia e usem roupas leves e confortáveis.

“A gente recomenda que os eleitores, ao saírem para votar, usem roupas leves para enfrentar esse B-R-O-Bró e levem também uma garrafinha d'água”, orientou Hugo Leite, chefe de Orientação das Zonas Eleitorais do TRE-PI, em entrevista à TV Clube.

Os eleitores também podem consultar a situação das filas antes de sair de casa. A ferramenta Kiwi permite acompanhar o movimento nas seções eleitorais , com atualização a cada 15 minutos, das 9h às 15h. A consulta pode ser feita no site do TRE-PI, com os números da zona e da seção eleitoral.

articles.body:

O Fato ou Fake , serviço de checagens do Grupo Globo , verificou declarações dos candidatos Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) e Lula ( PT ) nas entrevistas à TV Globo e no debate da Band, no domingo (18).

Para o debate da Globo desta sexta-feira (23), o Fato ou Fake preparou uma cobertura especial para verificar as declarações de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro .

Uma equipe de mais de 30 jornalistas do Grupo Globo vai trabalhar em conjunto para dar agilidade ao processo, sem abrir mão do rigor na apuração.

Como nas eleições municipais de 2024, as primeiras checagens serão publicadas durante o debate no g1 e nos sites dos jornais "O Globo" , "Valor Econômico" e "Extra" e da rádio CBN . O trabalho vai continuar pela madrugada, até que toda a apuração seja concluída.

A GloboNews terá um programa especial que vai ao ar logo após o debate e vai mostrar as checagens realizadas pela equipe do Fato ou Fake .

Criado em 2018, o Fato ou Fake reúne profissionais das sete redações do Grupo Globo — TV Globo , g1 , GloboNews , "O Globo" , "Valor" , "Extra" e CBN — e checa declarações de candidatos durante debates desde as eleições presidenciais de 2018.

Repórteres e editores acompanham o debate ao vivo e selecionam as declarações que pode ser verificadas com base em dados e informações objetivas. Opiniões, ofensas e projeções sobre o futuro não são checadas.

Com apoio da tecnologia e sob supervisão de jornalistas, a decupagem de todas as falas é gerada em tempo real, para garantir que a análise esteja baseada exatamente no que disseram os candidatos, palavra por palavra.

As falas dos candidatos são selecionadas e distribuídas, uma para cada repórter. Esse trabalho é contínuo durante todo o debate.

Para classificar as declarações, o Fato ou Fake usa três selos: #FATO , #NÃOÉBEMASSIM e #FAKE .

Cada checagem apresenta o passo a passo da apuração, com transparência sobre as fontes consultadas. Algumas declarações permitem uma checagem rápida, pelos dados oficiais ou públicos em bancos de dados acessíveis rapidamente. Outras exigem mais tempo, com entrevistas de autoridades ou especialistas no assunto e análises mais aprofundadas.

À medida que as novas checagens são concluídas, a reportagem é atualizada com os resultados.

Desde que foi criado, em 2018, o Fato ou Fake faz checagens diárias de informações. Em anos eleitorais, também analisa debates e entrevistas com os candidatos.

Neste ano, foram checadas, em agosto, as entrevistas concedidas pelos candidatos à Presidência ao g1 e à GloboNews , além de sabatinas promovidas por "O Globo" , "Valor" e CBN com os presidenciáveis e com candidatos aos governos de São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro.

articles.title: Moradores do RJ terão transporte público gratuito no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida busca facilitar o deslocamento da população até os locais de votação.
articles.summary: O transporte gratuito no Rio para o 2º turno das Eleições 2026 vale para ônibus, BRT e VLT das 6h às 20h, facilitando o acesso aos locais de votação.
articles.body:
Moradores do RJ terão transporte gratuito neste domingo — Foto: Tânia Rêgo / Agência Brasil

Os eleitores do Rio de Janeiro terão transporte público gratuito novamente no dia de votação do segundo turno, no próximo domingo (25). A gratuidade também foi oferecida no primeiro turno.

A iniciativa busca facilitar o deslocamento dos eleitores até os locais de votação, das 6h às 20h.

Na cidade do Rio, de acordo com a Secretaria Municipal de Transportes (SMTR), a medida vale para ônibus municipais, BRT, VLT, cabritinhos e vans ao longo do dia, com ampliação de horários e viagens extras.

Por sua vez, barcas, trens, metrô e ônibus intermunicipais vão circular com a oferta ajustada à demanda estimada ao longo do dia.

A gratuidade atende às Resoluções TSE nº 23.751/2026 e TRE-RJ nº 1.404/2026, que estabelecem a oferta gratuita de transporte coletivo urbano e intermunicipal nos dias de votação.

O sistema terá uma operação especial, com 340 viagens, 83% a mais que as 186 previstas na programação regular de domingo. Ao todo, serão 154 viagens adicionais para atender aos passageiros que vão se deslocar para suas zonas eleitorais.

Haverá aumento da circulação nos ramais Santa Cruz, Japeri, Saracuruna e Belford Roxo e também reforço nas extensões Paracambi e Guapimirim. O ramal Deodoro será atendido pelos trens dos ramais Japeri e Santa Cruz, que circularão como paradores.

A operação terá opções ampliadas ao longo do dia, com viagens mais cedo e partidas até mais tarde no retorno, incluindo a extensão de Paracambi.

O sistema aquaviário vai adotar a mesma grade de dias úteis para este domingo. A única exceção será a linha Praça XV–Paquetá, que manterá a grade de fins de semana e feriados, já que oferece uma viagem a mais.

As linhas 1 e 4 seguirão o trajeto entre Uruguai e Jardim Oceânico/Barra da Tijuca. Já a Linha 2 vai operar entre Pavuna e Botafogo; e a transferência entre as linhas 1 e 2 poderá ser feita no trecho entre as estações Central do Brasil/Centro e Botafogo. Também haverá trens extras para suprir o aumento da demanda e reforço no efetivo das equipes.

articles.title: Built in 1584 and abandoned in the 18th century, a roofless Scottish castle with original fireplaces and staircases is on sale for £120,000
articles.summary: A roofless Scottish castle that has stood for centuries is back on the market for offers over £120,000.
articles.body: A roofless Scottish castle that has stood for centuries is back on the market for offers over £120,000. Baltersan Castle, near Maybole in Ayrshire, was built in 1584 and deserted around the middle of the 18th century. Despite its long period without a roof, much of the Category A-listed building remains intact, including original fireplaces, staircases, floor levels and window openings.The castle occupies 0.75 acres of land, around 10 miles from Ayr and 45 miles from Glasgow. Architect and designer Charles Rennie Mackintosh sketched the building in 1895, while poets Robert Burns and John Keats also visited it. According to The Scottish Sun, the property is being marketed as a rare restoration opportunity.Baltersan Castle: The 16th-century Scottish tower house on saleBaltersan Castle is being offered for offers over £120,000, a price lower than many flats in Edinburgh and Glasgow. The property is a roofless, Category A-listed building near Maybole in Ayrshire. It comes with 0.75 acres of land and lies around 10 miles from Ayr and 45 miles from Glasgow. Selling agent Galbraith described it as an “exceptional” L-plan tower house with “national architectural and historic significance”.The agent also called the sale a “unique opportunity” to buy and restore one of the region’s most important historic buildings. However, planning consent for rebuilding and converting the tower house has expired.Baltersan Castle was constructed in 1584 by John Kennedy of Pennyglen and his wife, Margaret Cathcart. The Kennedys were a distinguished family in the Carrick area. The building is described as an L-plan tower house, and the agent describes it as a building of “national architectural and historic significance.” The structure was deserted around the middle of the 18th century. Despite that long period of abandonment, much of the building remains intact, including its original architectural details.A roofless structure still preserves centuries-old architectural detailsAlthough Baltersan Castle has stood without a roof for centuries, much of its original structure remains intact. The Category A-listed building retains its original fireplaces and staircases, along with its floor levels, roof geometry and window openings.The property also comes with 0.75 acres of land. According to the selling agent, the castle has retained a “remarkable degree” of structural integrity despite its long period of abandonment.Poets and a designer are among the notable figures linked to the castleBaltersan Castle attracted the attention of architect and designer Charles Rennie Mackintosh, who sketched the building in 1895 while holidaying in the area. The castle was also visited by poets Robert Burns and John Keats.In 2024, it emerged that the castle was in line for a £2 million restoration. It had previously been purchased by Italian computer engineer Angelo Ovidi for an undisclosed fee, with plans to restore the structure. The property is now back on the market, but planning consent for rebuilding and conversion has expired.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available information. articles.title: In 1864, Abraham Lincoln donated a signed photograph to help Union soldiers' families; generations later, it surfaced in an old desk with a forgotten newspaper clipping and sold for $149,020 at auction
articles.summary: Some historical treasures spend decades behind glass, carefully catalogued and admired.
articles.body: Some historical treasures spend decades behind glass, carefully catalogued and admired. Others wait quietly in forgotten corners of family homes, their significance hidden until an unexpected discovery brings the past back to life. A signed photograph of Abraham Lincoln followed the latter path, surviving for generations in a Massachusetts family before emerging with an old newspaper clipping that helped establish its remarkable history. The portrait eventually sold at auction for $149,020, states an auction report by RR Auction.A photograph with a wartime purposeAccording to the auction report, the photograph, known as Lincoln's Penny Profile, captures the 16th US president in a right-facing profile. Measuring 2.25 by 4 inches, the carte-de-visite portrait was taken on February 9, 1864, by Anthony Berger at Mathew Brady's photographic studio in Washington.The image became one of Lincoln's most recognisable likenesses and later served as the principal photographic reference for Victor David Brenner's design of the Lincoln cent. The same photographic sitting also produced the portrait that would eventually be adapted for the five-dollar bill.This particular example carries an additional distinction: Lincoln's signature appears in ink at the bottom, while an inscription on the reverse records its original purpose, adds the description of the portrait.Supporting Union soldiers' familiesAs per the report, in December 1864, as the American Civil War continued, Lincoln contributed six signed photographic portraits to the Soldiers' Aid Society of Westford, Massachusetts. The photographs were intended for sale at a fundraising event held on December 14, with proceeds supporting the families of local Union soldiers.Unable to provide federal funds directly to the organisation, Lincoln offered something of personal and historical value instead. The signed portraits became part of an effort to raise money for those bearing the cost of the war at home.The inscription on the reverse of the photograph confirms its connection to the Westford benefit, making it more than a presidential portrait. It is a surviving record of a wartime charitable initiative, adds the online report.A forgotten clipping reveals its historyAs per the description, the photograph is believed to have been acquired at the fundraising event by Charles G. Sargent, a prominent Westford industrialist and civic leader. It subsequently passed to his son, Allan C. Sargent, who was known for his preservation work and involvement in historical organisations.The portrait remained within the family for roughly a century before its significance was brought back into focus. An accompanying newspaper clipping from 1924 documented Lincoln's donation of the six photographs and affirmed the authenticity of his signature, adds the report.The clipping was discovered at the back of an old frame when the photograph resurfaced in a desk, providing a valuable link between the object and its original purpose.A rare piece of American historyThe photograph, presented in very good to fine condition with minor signs of age, was authenticated by PSA/DNA and accompanied by documentation detailing its provenance. Its eventual sale for $149,020 reflects the appeal of an object that combines presidential history, photographic significance and a documented connection to Civil War-era philanthropy.Images Courtesy: RR AuctionYou use AI every day. articles.title: Army to unveil new land warfare doctrine: What may change and why it matters
articles.summary: The army is about to get a new land warfare doctrine.
articles.body: The army is about to get a new land warfare doctrine. Defence minister Rajnath Singh will release it on Friday, the third and final day of the biannual Army Commanders' Conference, the first under General Dhiraj Seth as Army chief. The three-day meeting brings together the commanders-in-chief of the army's six operational and one training command and the principal staff officers at Army Headquarters. The defence ministry says the doctrine will give the force an overarching framework for the changing character of war, at a time when drones, precision strikes and networked operations are deciding more and more battles.The last land warfare doctrine was released in December 2018, about a year and a half after the joint doctrine of the armed forces of April 2017. Earlier editions came out in 1998 and 2004. The 2018 document dealt with the geostrategic environment, the spectrum of conflict, hybrid warfare, multi-front capability, surveillance, precision strike, information warfare, space warfare and special forces, and it was meant to form the basis for strategies on the northern and western fronts. The new version is expected to cover how operations are integrated across the conventional domains and newer ones such as cyber, space and electronic warfare, and the growing use of unmanned platforms and artificial intelligence in surveillance, targeting and decision-making.A good deal has happened since 2018. The army has been through a long stand-off with China along the Line of Actual Control. In May 2025, Operation Sindoor showed what long-range precision fire against targets across the border looks like. On May 7, India announced strikes on nine terrorist infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir and the army took on seven of them, using artillery and precision-guided munitions, including loitering munitions. At the same time, the wars in Ukraine and West Asia have brought drones, loitering munitions, ballistic and cruise missiles, electronic warfare and integrated air defence to the fore. Counter-insurgency operations in Jammu and Kashmir and the north-east have carried on throughout.The doctrine will be read against two fronts. In the north, the stand-off with China has made rapid mobilisation, high-altitude logistics and round-the-clock surveillance a priority. In the west, the Army has to deal with conventional formations, drones, missiles and cross-border attacks.The lessons from Ukraine and West Asia are also expected to feature. Drones and loitering munitions now handle reconnaissance, target acquisition and attack, while electronic warfare can knock out communications, navigation and command networks. With constant surveillance overhead, troops and vehicles find it harder to move unseen, which makes camouflage, deception, dispersal and mobility matter more. Ballistic and cruise missiles can hit headquarters, airfields, ammunition depots and supply points far behind the front line, so the Army has to think about how to protect them and how to keep communications going when networks are jammed or damaged. Artificial intelligence and digital command systems can speed up the way information is processed and shared, but they need reliable data, secure networks and trained people to work.The Integrated Defence Services issued its Joint Doctrine for Multi-Domain Operations in August 2025, a framework for bringing together land, air, maritime, space, cyber and information capabilities. For the army, that could mean combining satellite imagery, drone feeds, electronic intelligence, artillery targeting and air support to find and engage an enemy. The test is whether the right information reaches the right commander quickly, and whether the three services can work together when an adversary goes after communications, navigation or surveillance systems before attacking.The Army is also changing its own structure, and that may show up in the new document. Integrated Battle Groups bring combat and support elements under one commander for faster mobilisation. Bhairav battalions are light, mobile forces for reconnaissance and rapid response. Shaktibaan regiments and Divyastra batteries add drones, loitering munitions and precision strike, and Ashni platoons give infantry battalions their own drone capability.

articles.title: CM Devendra Fadnavis announces mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port, seeks Centre’s nod for 2,500-5,000 acres in Maharashtra

articles.body: MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port and urged the Centre to approve the project, for which the state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres.Speaking at the inauguration of Indochem in Goregaon, Fadnavis said the state government would make the land available for the proposed park and asked the Centre to sanction the project.The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.Union minister for chemicals and fertilisers JP Nadda said the Centre had already announced the Bhavya Rasayan scheme in the Union Budget. articles.title: In 2000, Durham repairman Gene Dillard began filling his yard with metal art; 15 years later, he started a mosaic home with hand tools, and neighbors gave tours
articles.summary: Discover the fascinating story of Gene Dillard, a former repairman who transformed his home into a stunning mosaic art piece in Durham, North Carolina. Uncover the creativity, inspiration, and community interactions behind this unique project.
articles.body: Most people who spend their working lives repairing other people’s equipment do not expect to spend retirement building an elaborate work of folk art. Perhaps a veggie patch in the back or a fishing pole. Few grab a pair of tile nippers and a bucket of shattered mirrors. On Elgin Street in Durham, North Carolina, Gene Dillard began filling his yard with metal sculptures around 2000 and started covering his house with mosaics around 2015, according to a PBS North Carolina profile. Dillard says he had never made art before taking on the project and had spent his working life as a repairman. The SPACES archives document the home’s mirror-covered exterior, backyard spaceship, pottery fence, and yard sculptures. None of it was meant as a business. Dillard says he doesn't sell his art and has manufactured most of it with modest hand tools.From repair work to mosaic artDillard was a repairman by trade and spent a good part of his working life maintaining scientific and restaurant supplies, according to Indy Week. He moved from San Diego to North Carolina in the 1980s and settled in Durham’s Northgate Park district. He tells us that he moved into the Elgin Street residence about the year 2000 and that is when the garden began to transform.The first were metallic. Dillard made a sea monster out of rebar that holds his mailbox, a surfer riding a wave down the front lawn, and a rainbow mermaid observing from the right. He has remarked that a first major mosaic, done together with a friend, got under his skin and he has been hooked on the craft ever since. He also said he likes the repetitive motion of the job, which helps explain why the project never ceased.Mirrors, pottery, and a spaceship in the backyardIn 2015, Dillard grew tired of making yard sculptures and began covering his house and garage with mosaics. He covered the walls of the front and driveway with pieces of mirror, first in winding vines that soon sprung from the wall in three-dimensional chunks. By 2017 he’d finished three walls of the home, three of the garage, and it was all cut with handheld tile nippers.In the backyard, Dillard built a spaceship from two-inch-square metal tubes welded together and wrapped in rebar. Green, blue and amber bottles cover the structure, filtering colored light into its interior at different times of day. Around it, a fence he completed over three years during the COVID quarantine holds pottery donated by friends and guests. Many works are presented with the potter’s name facing outward, a reference to craftspeople whose signatures are often unseen. Seven faces, including a Cyclops, a King, a Queen and a Knight, are made of rebar and cement and studded with shards, bottles and one unopened bottle of Jack Daniels. Within, each large window has its own mosaic valance, doors are trimmed in a matching daisy pattern, and the entryway over the front door has been converted to a double-height opening. Online maps label the address as Gene Dillard’s Fantasy Land.Dillard has been forthright about the source of the urge. He cited a few self-taught craftsmen as his influence in a 2017 interview with the Strange Carolinas travel site, including Minnie Evans, whose drawings he adores, and Henry Warren, whose small village in Prospect Hill he dubbed his personal Mecca. Warren’s Shangri-La is a town of 27 stone structures, which the retired tobacco farmer created on his own, commencing in 1968, the state tourism portal VisitNC says.Calling on a private residenceDillard says his neighbors have been supportive. In a PBS North Carolina feature about the house, one individual interviewed stated visitors sometimes feel overwhelmed by it and others are reluctant to come up the driveway, so they wanted a handout that points out minor details people might otherwise miss.SPACES describes the front and back yards as open to the public at all hours and claims Dillard is pleased to chat with guests if he happens to be there during the day. The inside of the house is his living space, and it is still a private property on a residential street, so a quiet visit and pleasant wave go a long way. The house is at 2706 Elgin St., in Northgate Park.And this is just the beginning. In winter 2024, the mosaic face of the chimney fell off, and Dillard wants to create a replacement. He's also got a wizard sculpture coming up that will have a lamp to light up his yard at night. The mosaic-covered exterior remains an evolving work of folk art, visible to passersby while the house itself remains a private residence.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2014, Sofía Vergara bought a Beverly Hills villa for $10.6 million; after renovating it and asking $19.6 million in 2022, the 11,000-square-foot estate finally sold for $13.7 million after nearly two years
articles.summary: Hollywood actor Sofía Vergara sold her Tuscan-style Beverly Hills estate for $13.7 million after nearly two years on the market.
articles.body: Hollywood actor Sofía Vergara sold her Tuscan-style Beverly Hills estate for $13.7 million after nearly two years on the market. Vergara bought the property for $10.6 million in 2014, renovated it with her then-husband Joe Manganiello, and initially listed it for $19.6 million in July 2022. As reported by Architectural Digest, the sale was reported on April 25, 2024, after the couple had reduced the asking price several times. The final price was nearly $6 million below the original listing price, but $3.1 million above the amount Vergara had paid for the home in 2014. The estate covers around 11,000 square feet and has seven bedrooms and 11 bathrooms. It sits on a plot of just over half an acre, behind gates and tall hedges.A $19.6 million asking price that kept fallingWhen Vergara and Manganiello put the property on the market in July 2022, they asked $19.6 million for it. In a 2022 report by the Los Angeles Times, the price was nearly double the $10.6 million paid for the property in 2014. The couple had already moved to a larger home in the Beverly Park neighbourhood in 2020. The new listing offered more than 11,000 square feet of living space, with a gym, movie theatre, wine cellar and wet bar. After the house remained unsold for about a year, the asking price was reduced to $17.99 million in the summer of 2023, according to Architectural Digest. It was subsequently listed again in early 2024 for around $13.9 million. The property eventually sold for $13.7 million.Inside the Tuscan-style estateThe home was built in 2006 and has a design inspired by Tuscan villas. As reported by the Los Angeles Times, the interior features neutral colours in the main living areas, while black accents appear in the office, theatre and bar. A spiral staircase connects the two levels, and the entrance has a rotunda-topped foyer. The formal living room features a large stone fireplace. The kitchen has a central island and dual sinks, while French doors connect the main living areas to the garden.The backyard includes a swimming pool, spa, several patios and a covered outdoor sitting area. Tall hedges and lawns provide privacy around the property. As reported by Architectural Digest, all seven bedrooms have en-suite bathrooms. The primary bedroom also has an outdoor patio with a stone fireplace and seating. Other features include a wet bar, a wine cellar that can hold 3,000 bottles, a wine-tasting room, a gym and a large home theatre with dark-wood detailing.Renovations before the saleVergara and Manganiello worked with Los Angeles designer Jennifer Bevan to remodel the home. In a July 2022 report, Architectural Digest described the renovation as a complete redesign, highlighting the high ceilings, dark-wood details and statement chandeliers. The couple’s decision to sell followed their move to a larger Beverly Park property. According to Architectural Digest, the 17,000-square-foot home had undergone two years of renovation before it was ready for them to move in. The Beverly Hills estate was therefore no longer their main home when they began trying to sell it.What the final sale price meansThe $13.7 million sale price was $5.9 million below the original $19.6 million asking price. However, compared with the $10.6 million purchase price in 2014, the sale represented a difference of $3.1 million before accounting for renovation costs, taxes, transaction fees and other expenses. The final figure was also slightly below the last reported asking price of $13.9 million. Vergara, best known for playing Gloria Delgado-Pritchett in the television comedy ‘Modern Family,’ was also serving as a judge on America’s Got Talent at the time of the 2022 listing, according to the Los Angeles Times. After nearly two years of attempted sale, the Beverly Hills villa finally changed hands in April 2024 for $13.7 million.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Rival factions, civil war & shadow of terror: Why Libya is still broken 15 years after Gaddafi's bloody end
articles.summary: Muammar Gaddafi's 42-year rule over Libya ended violently near his hometown of Sirte on October 20, 2011, when opposition fighters captured and killed him.
articles.body: Muammar Gaddafi's 42-year rule over Libya ended violently near his hometown of Sirte on October 20, 2011, when opposition fighters captured and killed him.His death marked the culmination of an uprising that began months earlier and was bolstered by a Nato-led military intervention. But the fall of one of Africa's longest-serving rulers did not bring the oil-rich North African country the stability many Libyans had hoped for.Fifteen years later, Libya remains divided between rival political administrations and competing centres of military power. Although a unified national budget was approved in April 2026 and a United Nations-backed agreement in August set out steps towards long-delayed elections, the country continues to struggle with political fragmentation, armed groups and disputes over state resources.The question, therefore, is not just how Gaddafi fell, but why his removal failed to bring stability to Libya.Why Gaddafi's regime fellThe uprising against Muammar Gaddafi began in February 2011, amid the Arab Spring protests that had toppled long-serving rulers in Tunisia and Egypt.Protests erupted in Benghazi on February 15, following the arrest of government critics, including a lawyer representing families of prisoners killed in the 1996 Abu Salim prison massacre. Libyan security forces responded with tear gas, batons and violence against demonstrators.The crackdown escalated the protests into an armed rebellion, with opposition forces taking control of parts of eastern Libya. On February 26, the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 1970, imposing sanctions and referring the situation to the International Criminal Court.On March 17, it adopted Resolution 1973, authorising member states to take “all necessary measures” to protect civilians. Nato took command of the military operation on March 31, enforcing an arms embargo and no-fly zone and conducting military operations.Tripoli fell to opposition forces on August 21, 2011, forcing Gaddafi's regime out of the capital. Two months later, as rebels overran his hometown of Sirte, Gaddafi attempted to flee in a convoy that came under Nato air strikes.He was captured alive by fighters from Misrata on October 20 and killed shortly afterwards. A subsequent Human Rights Watch investigation found evidence that he had been beaten and wounded after his capture, raising questions over a possible extrajudicial killing.What happened to Libya after Gaddafi's deathGaddafi's death in October 2011 left Libya facing the challenge of building a new political system while armed groups that had fought his regime retained their weapons and influence.The National Transitional Council oversaw the transition before handing power to an elected General National Congress in August 2012. However, successive governments struggled to bring militias under state control, while political divisions and insecurity continued to deepen.Libya's civil war deepens the divideLibya descended into a full-scale civil war in 2014, as political divisions and rival armed groups fractured the country.In May that year, military commander Khalifa Haftar launched Operation Dignity against Islamist militant groups and other opponents in eastern Libya, including Benghazi. Two months later, a separate campaign known as Libya Dawn emerged in western Libya, as Misrata-based armed groups and their allies fought rival factions, particularly over control of Tripoli International Airport.The fighting left Libya divided between rival political and military camps in the east and west, each establishing its own institutions and command structures.The security vacuum also allowed Islamic State (ISIS) to expand its presence. The group established a foothold in Derna before consolidating control over Sirte in 2015, turning Gaddafi's hometown into its main stronghold in Libya.ISIS imposed its rule through public executions, kidnappings and intimidation, while recruiting local fighters and former regime personnel.The United Nations Security Council warned in 2015 that the group's growing presence, alongside other extremist organisations, posed a serious threat to Libya and the wider region.In December 2015, a UN-brokered political agreement paved the way for the Government of National Accord, intended to reunify Libya's institutions. But the arrangement struggled to establish authority across the country. However, forces aligned with the internationally recognised government, supported by US air strikes, drove ISIS from Sirte in December 2016.Haftar's forces eventually launched an offensive against Tripoli in April 2019. The United Arab Emirates and Egypt supported Haftar's eastern camp, while Turkey provided crucial military support to Tripoli-aligned forces. Russia also backed Haftar's forces, including through personnel linked to the Wagner Group. These competing external interests reinforced Libya's internal divisions and complicated efforts to reach a political settlement.A UN-backed ceasefire in October 2020 halted large-scale fighting between the principal camps, but rival administrations and competing security structures endured.Libya after 2020The ceasefire of October 2020 ended large-scale fighting between Libya's rival eastern and western camps, but failed to reunify the country's political and military institutions.A UN-backed process installed Abdul Hamid Dbeibah as head of the Government of National Unity (GNU) in 2021, with elections intended to end the transitional period. The vote was postponed indefinitely amid disputes over electoral laws and candidate eligibility.In 2022, the eastern-based House of Representatives appointed a rival administration, leaving Libya divided between competing governments.The division remains central to Libya's current political and military landscape.The GNU, led by Dbeibah, operates from Tripoli in the west, while an eastern-based administration led by Osama Hamad is backed by the House of Representatives and Khalifa Haftar's Libyan Arab Armed Forces, also known as the Libyan National Army.Haftar's forces control much of eastern Libya and have expanded their influence and security presence in parts of the south.Western Libya, meanwhile, remains divided among government-aligned and other armed formations.Although the main east-west front has remained largely quiet since the ceasefire, rival military structures and local militia rivalries continue to pose security risks.The US Congressional Research Service reported in July 2026 that Haftar's forces had expanded their influence in the south and strengthened their military capabilities, including through drones.The political deadlock has also complicated efforts to organise national elections.In August 2026, a UN-facilitated agreement set out steps to reform the High National Elections Commission and address outstanding issues in the legal framework for presidential and parliamentary elections. The parties committed to work towards holding the vote within 24 months, rather than agreeing on a fixed election date.However, the process has encountered fresh resistance.In an October 14 briefing to the UN Security Council, UN Special Representative Hanna S. Tetteh said the House of Representatives had endorsed the agreement, but the High State Council rejected it on October 5, citing concerns over constitutional, legal and consensual procedures.The setback underlines how even a negotiated roadmap can become another point of contention between rival institutions.Oil wealth, economic pressure and failing public servicesDespite possessing Africa's largest proven oil reserves, Libya continues to face serious economic and fiscal vulnerabilities. Oil remains the backbone of its economy, accounting for 65 per cent of GDP, 93 per cent of exports and 72 per cent of government revenue in 2024, according to the World Bank.Production recovery has supported economic growth, but dependence on hydrocarbons leaves public finances exposed to disruptions caused by political disputes, fluctuating oil output and weak fiscal management.The International Monetary Fund warned in April 2026 that Libya's fiscal position had become increasingly vulnerable, estimating the budget deficit at around 30 per cent of GDP in 2025 and public debt at 146 per cent of GDP over the preceding two years. The IMF called for urgent fiscal adjustment to ease pressure on foreign exchange reserves, the dinar and inflation.In April, representatives of Libya's House of Representatives and High Council of State agreed to a unified national budget worth 190 billion Libyan dinars, or about $29.95 billion. It was the first such agreement since 2013.Central Bank Governor Naji Issa, who supervised the signing, described it as “a clear declaration that Libya is capable of overcoming its differences when a unified vision for its future is forged”.The agreement was intended to improve financial coordination and support development spending across the country, although its implementation remains a separate test. The deal marked progress in financial coordination, but it did not resolve the political divisions underpinning the country's wider crisis.The consequences of fragmentation are particularly visible in public services and infrastructure. The September 2023 floods that devastated Derna exposed failures in infrastructure maintenance, disaster preparedness and public accountability.Public services remain weak despite the country's oil wealth. The World Bank has highlighted shortcomings in healthcare, education, water and electricity provision, alongside high unemployment, corruption concerns and an underdeveloped private sector.These problems continue to constrain Libya's development, even as oil revenues offer the country significant financial resources.Fragile peace, uncertain futureAlthough Libya has avoided a return to full-scale civil war since the 2020 ceasefire, rival military structures, powerful armed groups and foreign involvement continue to threaten stability.Briefing the UN Security Council on October 14, Tetteh warned that “institutional and political fragmentation have continued to impact negatively on the economic and security situation in the country”.She said many Libyans were seeing their purchasing power eroded by rising food prices, a weaker dinar and inflation above 14 per cent, while access to essential public services remained unreliable.Tetteh also cautioned that the path to stability remained difficult, saying, “The path to a stable, unified, and prosperous Libya remains long, but our destination remains within reach.” She urged Libyan political actors to demonstrate the flexibility and political will needed to reach common ground.Fifteen years after Gaddafi's death, Libya's challenge is no longer simply to prevent another civil war. It is to build a state capable of controlling armed groups, managing oil revenues transparently and delivering reliable public services.The election roadmap and unified budget offer potential steps towards greater stability, but neither guarantees lasting peace. Libya's future will depend on whether rival leaders can turn these commitments into a functioning political settlement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Another tiger captured near Gudalur in the Nilgiris
articles.summary: UDHAGAMANDALAM: A tiger that is suspected to have preyed on livestock in and around O-Valley near Gudalur in the Nilgiris in the past few weeks was on
articles.body: UDHAGAMANDALAM: A tiger that is suspected to have preyed on livestock in and around O-Valley near Gudalur in the Nilgiris in the past few weeks was on Thursday found trapped in a cage set up by the forest department. The tiger, aged around 13 years, was trapped a month after another tiger, which is suspected to have killed two men, had been trapped in the same area by the forest department.Forest department personnel tied a goat inside the cage to lure the tiger that killed livestock. The tiger was found lying inside the cage in a semi-conscious state on Thursday morning. A forest department staff member wearing protective gear approached the animal, but it remained in the same condition. The tiger was subsequently shifted to a smaller cage for transportation.Gudalur forest range officer P Devaraj said the big cat was caught in their camera traps a couple of times in the last few weeks. “Deep wounds were found on its face. The animal looked very tired. Generally, wounds caused by infighting would heal. But this 13-year-old tiger was found to be very tired. We are planning to shift it to Vandalur zoo in Chennai. Once an official order is issued, it will be moved,” he said.On Sept 18, the forest department trapped a tiger that is suspected to have killed two men. The animal was captured following a 29-day search operation. articles.title: Govt nod to stipend hike for junior resident doctors, DNB trainees
articles.summary: Jharkhand govt approves stipend hike for junior resident doctors in govt medical colleges; proposal initiated to revise DNB trainee stipends at RINPAS.
articles.body: Ranchi: In a move aimed at boosting doctors’ morale and strengthening healthcare services, the state health department on Thursday announced an increase in the monthly stipend of junior resident (academic) doctors in govt medical colleges and hospitals, while also initiating action to revise stipends for DNB trainees at the Ranchi Institute of Neuro-Psychiatry and Allied Sciences (RINPAS), Kanke.Under a govt resolution dated April 27, 2026, the stipend for first-year junior residents has been raised from Rs 54,500 to Rs 70,000 per month, for second-year residents from Rs 58,500 to Rs 75,000, and for third-year residents from Rs 63,000 to Rs 80,000.The health department has also acted on a proposal to revise stipends for DNB trainees at RINPAS in line with prescribed norms. Under the proposed structure, broad speciality DNB trainees would receive a minimum stipend of Rs 43,000, Rs 45,000 and Rs 47,000 per month in the first, second and third years respectively. Post-diploma DNB trainees would be entitled to Rs 45,000 and Rs 47,000 per month during the first and second years of training.Health minister Irfan Ansari said, “The govt is committed to ensuring dignity and better working conditions for doctors as they are an integral part of our healthcare system.”The minister added that the govt’s priority was not only to increase stipends but also to improve healthcare infrastructure, provide modern equipment in hospitals and create better working conditions for medical professionals. “The revision would help attract and retain talented doctors in Jharkhand,” he said.Additional chief secretary, health, Ajoy Kumar Singh said the proposal had been approved following the minister’s directions. “The objective is to boost the morale of both junior and senior doctors and provide them with better working conditions. The govt has consistently taken steps to improve salaries and stipends of medical professionals,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Harish blames Congress for drought, crop losses on 12L acres across state
articles.summary: Harish Rao blames Telangana Congress govt for “drought-created” crop losses on 12 lakh acres, citing poor irrigation and power; seeks drought declaration and aid.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Former minister T Harish Rao alleged that Telangana is facing a “Congress-created drought” due to the state govt’s failure to ensure adequate irrigation and power supply, resulting in crops drying up on nearly 12 lakh acres across the state.He demanded that the state govt immediately declare drought-hit mandals, provide compensation for crop losses, release ₹12,000 in assistance to agricultural labourers, ensure 24-hour quality power supply, operate irrigation projects round the clock, and take measures to address drinking water shortages across the state.After visiting drought-hit paddy fields in Burugupalli village, Gajwel mandal, Siddipet district, on Thursday, Harish met with affected farmers. He reviewed crop losses due to a lack of water and electricity. He accused the Congress govt of ignoring repeated warnings from scientists and agricultural experts about possible drought conditions due to El Nino and of failing to take preventive measures in time.Addressing reporters, Harish said farmers in several districts, including Adilabad, Karimnagar, Nalgonda, Medak, Khammam and Mahabubnagar, had suffered severe crop losses. He alleged that the state govt had neither secured sufficient coal stocks nor purchased adequate power in advance, leading to an electricity shortage during the critical crop season. Instead of accepting responsibility, he said, the govt was attempting to blame officials for the crisis.The BRS leader also accused the Congress govt of not operating lift irrigation schemes such as Kannepalli, Devadula and Kalwakurthy at full capacity, resulting in irrigation shortages and widespread crop damage. He claimed that hundreds of acres in the Gajwel region alone had dried up just as crops were nearing harvest.Citing individual cases, Harish said several farmers had spent thousands of rupees on diesel generators to save their crops but still suffered heavy losses because of irregular power supply and low-voltage issues.Drawing comparisons with the previous BRS govt, he said uninterrupted power and irrigation facilities had helped farmers achieve record agricultural production even during difficult periods.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Iran reveals ‘offensive’ doctrine, US issues alert: Is war imminent?
articles.summary: US orders diplomatic staff out of Saudi Arabia amid escalating conflict and reports of potential US strikes on Iran.
articles.body:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) says renewed attacks by the United States could prompt Tehran to invade neighbouring countries and hit bases used in US military operations as part of its new “offensive” strategy.

The warning on Wednesday came amid escalating attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a global energy chokepoint, and uncertainty over diplomatic efforts to end the nearly eight-month war.

“Our defence doctrine was previously defensive; we used to say that if a country attacks us, we will respond. Now we say that if a country attacks us, we will both respond and launch an offensive,” IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebi said.

Washington ordered some diplomatic personnel to leave Saudi Arabia amid attacks from Yemen’s Houthis while US President Donald Trump has signalled that a decision on the conflict could come soon.

According to media reports, the US and Israel are planning potential attacks on Iran in the coming weeks.

As negotiations seem stalled and both sides exchange threats, could the region be heading towards another military escalation?

The IRGC on Wednesday announced a shift towards an “offensive and asymmetrical” defence doctrine, threatening to invade countries that launch attacks against it.

Mohebi said Tehran would no longer limit its military operations to retaliatory strikes.

Mohebi stressed that Iran’s missile stockpile has increased 1.5 times since the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025. He did not provide specific figures.

“The quality of the missiles has improved significantly, and their range, destructive power and accuracy in hitting targets have increased,” the spokesman said.

Moreover, Mohebi said Iranian forces were in the “stage of preparing to unveil the ‘father of all bombs’. This is something new for the enemy.”

Meanwhile, attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continued unabated.

The IRGC’s navy said on Thursday that four vessels it accused of being involved in illegal oil transfers were struck and caught fire in the northern Gulf. Three other vessels hit mines west of the strait, it added.

Before the war, one-fifth of the world’s oil and natural gas supplies passed through the Strait of Hormuz. While shipments through the strait are still below those levels, oil shipments from the region returned to pre-war levels last month as exporters found alternative ways to ship out their oil and gas, including using pipelines.

However, a flurry of recent attacks in the key waterway and the fighting between Yemen’s Houthis and its Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government, which has resulted in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, have once again sent oil prices surging. Brent crude climbed above $110 a barrel on Thursday amid fears of further disruptions to regional energy supplies.

Iran’s shift towards an offensive military doctrine reflects Tehran’s determination to make future US-Israeli attacks significantly more costly, according to analysts.

Negar Mortazavi, senior fellow at the Centre for International Policy, told Al Jazeera that Tehran was drawing lessons from the wars of 2025 and 2026 after its previous strategy of retaliation failed to prevent repeated attacks.

“Tehran now wants to establish a new equation: Any future attack on Iran will come at a much higher cost for the aggressors,” she told Al Jazeera.

Unable to match conventional US military capabilities, Iran is increasingly relying on asymmetric warfare, including missiles, drones and its leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, Mortazavi explained.

She said Tehran was pursuing a broader strategy aimed at imposing military, economic and political costs on Washington, including potentially influencing the November 3 US midterm elections.

“Iran wants to teach Washington a lesson: Attacking Iran comes with a high price, one that can even cost elections,” Mortazavi said, referring to US surveys that are predicting electoral losses for Trump’s Republican Party.

She added that Iranian officials were closely monitoring the elections, believing the economic fallout from the war could damage the Republican Party’s prospects of retaining control of Congress.

“The long-term objective is to establish deterrence so that future American administrations think twice before daring to attack Iran again,” she said.

Political analyst Rami Khouri said the doctrine was also intended to ensure that the consequences of attacks extend to the US, Israel and regional countries supporting their military operations.

“That’s one part of the strategy, that the suffering and the damage have to be equal and reciprocal,” Khouri, nonresident senior fellow at the Arab Center, told Al Jazeera.

Khouri argued that Tehran was also seeking to challenge what it views as longstanding Western domination of the region.

“The Iranians are actually working to try to end the colonial period,” he said.

He added that Iran’s strategy could extend the economic consequences of conflict far beyond the Middle East, affecting energy supplies, transportation, insurance costs and shipments of essential goods.

“The pain is going to go way beyond just the Middle East and Israel and the US and will hurt people in other parts of the world,” Khouri said.

What has the US said about resuming the war?

Trump has offered conflicting signals about Washington’s next steps.

On Wednesday, he said the US was no longer negotiating with Tehran and suggested developments were imminent. “We are going to have something one way or the other that’ll happen fairly soon,” he told reporters.

He also said Washington could end the war immediately but wanted a lasting outcome. “It’ll end very soon. We could leave now, but we want to make sure it lasts for a long time,” Trump said at a campaign rally in South Carolina.

Trump previously pledged not to attack Iran before the November 3 elections.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said this week that reaching a peace agreement is extremely difficult and insisted that Iran must stop targeting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

In recent weeks, Iran’s enrichment of uranium has re-emerged as a point of contention .

Rubio has maintained that Washington will reject any agreement allowing Iran to develop nuclear weapons, which require highly enriched uranium. “The United States will not support any deal that creates a pathway for Iran to ever have a nuclear weapon,” he said on Wednesday.

Tehran insisted its right to enrichment is guaranteed under the Non-Proliferation Treaty.

Iran has offered a seven-day plan to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington ending its blockade of Iranian ports, easing sanctions and unfreezing Iranian assets.

Meanwhile, the US Department of State on Wednesday ordered nonemergency personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia after recent Houthi attacks.

The US embassy in Riyadh has warned of further attacks while American officials told the Reuters news agency that family members could be withdrawn from other Gulf missions.

State Department spokesman Tommy Piggott said departure orders for mission personnel across the Gulf have not been ordered, saying the current orders were for “employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated on Sunday his pledge to topple Iran’s government, saying it was key to preventing it from rebuilding its nuclear programme and the “axis of resistance”, further raising prospects of an escalation.

Netanyahu made the comments as Israel’s longest-serving prime minister is locked in a tough battle to remain in power in Tuesday’s elections.

Analysts warned that renewed US-Israeli attacks on Iran are increasingly possible with both sides preparing for another confrontation despite the continued possibility of diplomacy.

“Another round of war seems to be approaching,” Mortazavi said.

“Both sides appear to be preparing for renewed confrontation while escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz increase the risk of a wider conflict,” she said.

Mortazavi added that the elections in the next two weeks in the US and Israel could influence the timing of military action but warned that the current trajectory appeared to favour escalation over negotiations.

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, on Wednesday said, “Everyone must know that any action against Iran comes at a cost.”

“If diplomacy can create this understanding, we prefer diplomacy, but if the war continues, Iran has the necessary means to sustain its response,” Rezaei said, according to the IRNA news agency.

Echoing Mortazavi, Khouri warned that another confrontation could be approaching although he said US threats might still be part of a negotiating strategy.

“I think imminent conflict is on the cards, but I don’t know if war is the right word to use,” Khouri told Al Jazeera.

He said renewed strikes could target Iran’s critical infrastructure, including electricity networks, transportation systems, bridges and essential services.

“We’re probably going to get some severe attacks on a few targets that will try to make life in Iran very difficult,” he said.

However, Khouri cautioned that Iran’s ability to withstand another major military offensive while inflicting comparable damage on its adversaries remained uncertain.

“It’s not clear if Iran has the ability to withstand major new assaults against it,” he said, while stressing that Tehran was unlikely to surrender to military pressure.

articles.title: Airbnb rule change frees guests from chores involving ‘significant effort’
articles.summary: Airbnb has revised its rules to reduce the tasks a host can expect a guest to perform at the end of their stay — and washing dishes has been wiped from the to-do list.
articles.body: Airbnb has revised its rules to reduce the tasks a host can expect a guest to perform at the end of their stay — and washing dishes has been wiped from the to-do list. Airbnb, which connects travelers with more than 5 million hosts globally, has advised hosts to choose from seven standard house rules that will be displayed prominently on the listing page. Hosts can set ground rules for maximum occupancy, quiet hours, and pets, as well as specify key return procedures and whether guests may hold events or host commercial photo shoots. The policy update, applicable to all reservations booked on or after November 20, is designed to streamline the Airbnb experience after a slew of customer complaints about unclear house rules and laborious demands by property hosts. “House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we’ve heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous and hard to manage,” an Airbnb spokesperson told CNN Thursday. “So we’ve redesigned them to make them easier to discover and clearer to set, alongside a new policy that keeps requests reasonable, with no surprises,” they added. Hosts remain free to detail more specific requests alongside the formulaic rules they’ve selected from Airbnb’s standard list, but those requests must be considered reasonable. Chores requiring “significant effort or time” that would typically be completed by a cleaner are off limits as guest requests, including stripping beds and taking out the trash. While hosts are no longer at liberty to instruct guests to wash and put dishes away, they may request that used dishes are placed in the sink upon their departure. Host-imposed fines are also prohibited, and guests are expected to work with hosts to reach a solution if a deeper issue, such as property damage, occurs. Transparency appears to be key under the new policy, as hosts must be upfront about their house rules at the time of booking and cannot add caveats later. Nor can hosts ask guests to enter a contract separate from the one they signed via Airbnb when they made their booking, except in limited circumstances. “Personally, I think it’s fantastic,” Minnesota mom Ellen, known online as Tall Mom Running, said in a video on social media. She said that during a previous Airbnb stay, she was sent a list of things to do the day before leaving the property and threatened with a fine if they were not completed. “It was an hour worth of work,” she laughed, adding: “An hour of cleaning … No thank-you, I don’t want to be doing that on vacation.” But not everyone is as thrilled about the policy amendment. “It’s not a matter of duty it’s about good manners,” Rossana Imbrogno, whose property in Rome has been adorned with the title of “guest favourite” on the site, said in a comment on social media. “I clean and strip the bed and trash the litter even if I stay in a hotel,” the “superhost” added.

articles.title: US accuses Canada of interference in midterm elections, Carney denies charges
articles.summary: The US Embassy in Ottawa has accused Canadian leaders of attempting to influence American politics ahead of the November midterm elections, escalating
articles.body: The US Embassy in Ottawa has accused Canadian leaders of attempting to influence American politics ahead of the November midterm elections, escalating tensions between the two neighbours amid an ongoing trade dispute under President Donald Trump’s administration.According to the BBC, the embassy released a fact sheet on Wednesday alleging that Canadian ministers and provincial premiers had openly discussed plans to influence American politics through official documents and public appearances. The document cited meetings with US Democratic leaders and calls for retaliatory tariffs targeting politically significant American states.The unsigned document singled out Canadian Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, Ontario Premier Doug Ford, Liberal MP Anthony Housefather and Bernadette Jordan, a former cabinet minister who now serves as Canada's consul general in Boston.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ford rejected the allegations, arguing that Ottawa's actions were a response to Washington's trade measures rather than an attempt to interfere in US elections.Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Carney said the US had initiated the trade actions against Canada and that his government had responded to protect Canadian jobs and businesses."We've responded to those to protect Canadian jobs, to protect Canadian companies and develop our economy," Carney said, adding that the measures were in the interests of Canadian workers, families and the country's economic future.Carney was announcing an aid package worth nearly C$9 billion to support businesses and workers affected by US tariffs. Joly and Ford were also present at the announcement.Ford said he had "no interest at all" in interfering in American elections, adding that his focus remained on Ontario and Canada."I'll tell you what the American people want. They want certainty, they want stability," Ford said, adding that American voters would decide the outcome of the midterm elections.Why US has accused Canada of election interferenceThe embassy's allegations focused partly on Canada's retaliatory tariffs against American goods. The measures were introduced in response to tariffs imposed by the Trump administration and have become a major source of friction between Washington and Ottawa.The fact sheet cited comments by Joly about targeting products from politically significant US states. In August, when Canada announced retaliatory tariffs, she said the measures were intended partly to exert political pressure on the US.The embassy also referred to Joly's response when asked what she expected from US tariff policy if Democrats won the midterm elections."That's exactly why I'm meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates," she said.Ontario Premier Ford had also urged Canada's federal government to consider further retaliatory tariffs on imports from states considered important to Trump's political support base.The document also highlighted Housefather's campaign activities with a Democratic candidate in Florida and alleged that Canada was the second-largest source of foreign nationals prosecuted in the US for fraudulent or illegal voting, citing figures from the US Department of Justice.It urged Canadians to refrain from attempting to participate in or influence American elections, stating that Americans should decide their own elections.Canada rejects allegations as tensions deepenJoly has repeatedly denied that Canada is interfering in US elections. Last week, she said her visits to the US were aimed at attracting investment from American companies and that she planned to continue those efforts.She also said Canadians would not accept similar interference in their own elections, according to the BBC.Earlier this month, US Ambassador to Canada Pete Hoekstra warned that American officials were closely monitoring Canadian politicians for signs of election interference. White House adviser Peter Navarro had also warned Canadians against interfering in the US midterms."Please, if you're on K Street, get the hell out of our country," Navarro said, referring to the Washington lobbying industry.The dispute comes as relations between the two countries have deteriorated over trade, tariffs and Trump's repeated remarks about making Canada the 51st US state.Carney has also pushed for Canada to reduce its economic dependence on the US. Speaking at a rally in Calgary ahead of a referendum on Alberta's separation from Canada, he joked that Washington might interpret his remarks as election interference."They might think that's election interference. They're a little touchy down there," Carney said.The November midterm elections will determine which party controls the US House of Representatives and Senate, potentially shaping the remainder of Trump's presidency and the administration's ability to advance its legislative agenda.Meanwhile, a petition calling for Hoekstra's removal over concerns that he has undermined Canada-US diplomatic relations has received more than 280,000 signatures.You use AI every day. articles.title: Former Scotland rugby international Tim Visser to go on trial charged with rape
articles.summary: Tim Visser is accused of controlling and abusive behaviour against a woman over a a 14-year period in Edinburgh and elsewhere.
articles.body:
A former Scotland rugby international is to go on trial accused of controlling, abusing and raping a woman.

The charges against Tim Visser span a 14-year period and are alleged to have happened in Edinburgh and elsewhere between 2010 and 2024.

Two of the four charges state that the 39 year-old, who has been capped 33 times by Scotland, raped the woman on various occasions.

These include claims he had sex with her after consent had been withdrawn.

A separate charge alleges that the ex-Newcastle Falcons, Edinburgh and Harlequins player repeatedly behaved in a threatening and abusive manner towards the woman.

Among the accusations are that Visser "took intimate images" of her without her consent.

He was said to have been aggressive, sent her unwanted calls and texts, demanded to know where she was and controlled her appearance, finances and what she wore and ate.

Prosecutors further claim Visser, from Milton Bridge, Midlothian, isolated the woman from family and friends and was physically violent.

A fourth charge says he engaged in a course of abusive behaviour against the woman on various occasions.

The accusation lists a total of 26 different claims.

A number of them are similar to the threatening behaviour allegation, but also include a string of sexual matters.

One is that he sent an intimate image of the woman to someone else.

The indictment goes on to state that the prosecution may present evidence about other matters dating back to 2004, but these are not formal charges at this stage.

They feature claims of physical and sexual incidents, threats and controlling behaviour.

At the High Court in Glasgow, Ian Duguid, defending, said: "It is a plea of not guilty to the indictment."

A trial was set for 12 January 2028 in Edinburgh.

The ex-rugby star was born in the Netherlands, but opted not to play for his home nation.

Instead he represented Scotland as a winger between 2012 and 2017 before he retired from the sport two years later.

articles.title: Macron blames ‘seditious’ far left for unrest as France bans some protests
articles.summary: Thursday’s planned demonstrations are outlawed in parts of Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble.
articles.body:
French authorities have barred demonstrations in several of the country’s largest cities, as President Emmanuel Macron blamed far-left groups for stoking violence during weekend protests .

The Paris Police Prefecture announced that Thursday’s protests would be banned in key parts of the city until 8pm (18:00 GMT). That includes areas near the presidential Elysee Palace, both houses of parliament, the city’s main train stations, as well as parts of downtown where looting occurred over the weekend.

A police source told the AFP news agency the ban was necessary due to organisers’ “inability to prevent violence and vandalism”.

Elsewhere in France, authorities also prohibited protests planned for Thursday in Lyon, Lille and Grenoble.

The restrictions come after more than half a million people gathered across France on Saturday in a protest that brought together students demanding better conditions in schools and groups denouncing high living costs. At least 2,500 people were arrested after riots broke out in several areas , with shops looted.

French President Emmanuel Macron blamed Saturday’s riots on what he called “seditious acts” by “ultra-left” groups, whom he accused of trying to “bring down the Republic”.

Speaking from the Elysee Palace on Thursday, Macron said France would ban all “illegitimate” protests in the coming days, while approved demonstrations led by organised groups like unions would be required to take alternative routes outside city centres to protect businesses .

He added that he would convene the country’s defence council on Friday to take further action.

Thursday’s planned protests were seen as a prelude to a large demonstration on Saturday, when activists from the “yellow vest” movement, whose demonstrations over fuel prices shook France in 2018 and 2019, are expected to join.

Some of those protests, including marches in Lyon, will also be banned, local authorities said.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, who met union representatives on Wednesday, said a “massive” security operation was planned for Saturday to prevent a repeat of the violence by small groups of rioters that had exposed shortcomings in security measures.

Meanwhile, Macron held a meeting with intelligence services, Lecornu and ministers on Thursday morning to obtain a detailed account of what went wrong over the weekend and review preparations for upcoming protests.

Union representatives said their meeting with Lecornu did not result in concrete proposals. They are now focusing on another big day of action scheduled for November 5, calling on private and public sector employees to join.

The education demonstrations first erupted last month in a high school in Creteil, southeast of Paris, over a lack of staff.

From there, class strikes, blockades and demonstrations spread to other Paris suburbs and then nationwide, including in smaller towns.

High school students have raised concerns about underfunded schools, dilapidated facilities and staff shortages, particularly in lower-income neighbourhoods.

The school demonstrations and blockades have morphed into larger protests over soaring living costs.

articles.title: Activists celebrate as Harding's Pits given protected status
articles.summary: Volunteers say they have been campaigning for 30 years to keep a wild space free from development.
articles.body:
Campaigners who have been trying to stop the development of a town's green space have celebrated it being given "village green status" by a council.

Harding's Pits, seven acres of land beside the River Great Ouse in King's Lynn, had previously been earmarked for a housing development and a supermarket before the Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk applied to Norfolk County Council for the status.

The Harding's Pits Community Association Group has campaigned for the past 30 years to keep the area as a leisure space.

Rick Morrish, 64, the director of the group, said it was a "really great decision... we've struggled to get the village green status for 30 years".

The application was considered by Norfolk County Council's Planning (Regulatory) Committee on Tuesday.

Morrish told Chris Goreham on BBC Radio Norfolk that "this year's administration got right behind" the cause and it would "give more legal status to protect the site... we're safeguarding it as a public open space".

Alexandra Kemp, an Independent councillor at the borough council, said she has held nine public events in favour of keeping Harding's Pits as a space for nature.

"After the long campaign that we fought since 2017 with residents to stop the Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk putting traffic on Harding's Way, the borough council's support is very important and now protects all of Harding's Pits west of Harding's Way," she said.

Kemp also campaigned with residents in July against a new car park that the borough council sought to build next to Harding's Pits.

Morrish said the Harding's Pits Association Group was formed in 2004, adding that the green space was originally a clay pit in the 19th Century, before being used as a landfill site.

"There is actually rubbish underneath the site," he added.

Harding's Pits was then turned into a public space in the early 1960s.

The site is currently used for dog walking, accessing King's Lynn town centre, picking fruit such as blackberries and for bird and wildlife spotting, Morrish said.

He told the BBC that "a hundred species of birds" had been recorded there and it was home to "three or four regular reptile residents, including a lot of lizards" who had enjoyed the warm temperatures this year.

"Within the town, this is quite a rare asset to have and that's why we think it's so important," he added.

He said the site has grown over the years, with a new community orchard and a national art project, where artists have planted a circle of oak trees.

Michael de Whalley, the cabinet member for climate change and biodiversity on Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk, said: "This is very welcome news for South Lynn and an important final step in a journey that the community has been pursuing for at least 30 years."

He added that local people valued and enjoyed places such as Harding's Pits and surrounding green spaces, where habitats could flourish.
